# Methods

You use [markdown](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html) to indicate formatting -- the most important formatting elements for your thesis/dissertation are [headings](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html). These will be most directly tied to the look of your graduate school formatted document.  

You should also familiarize yourself with cross--references -- they will help:

  1. reader [navigation](https://quarto.org/docs/books/book-crossrefs.html) of your paper
  2. management of [tables and figures](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/cross-references.html)
  
Regarding #1, see @sec-meh

Regarding #2, if you properly cross--reference your tables and figures, you will NOT need to do any manual renumbering or sequencing if (when) your advisor asks for a sequence swap.
